prompt: I'm trying to understand how kitty's terminal reflow system works internally. When the window is resized, text needs to be redistributed across the new dimensions while maintaining line continuations and cursor positions. I've noticed some edge cases where the reflow doesn't seem to preserve logical line boundaries correctly. Can you trace through the rewrap implementation in the C code, explain how it handles the interaction between the visible screen buffer and the scrollback history during resize, and identify any potential issues with how line continuation state is propagated between these two buffers? I need to understand the complete data flow from the resize entry point through the rewrap logic. Don't create or modify any files.
